name: Berenice (sister of Agrippa II)
title: The Herodian Princess
summary: Berenice was the daughter of Herod Agrippa I and sister to King Agrippa II. She was present with her brother when the apostle Paul defended himself in Caesarea, and she is known from history for her many marriages and her controversial relationship with the Roman general Titus.

keyEvents.title: Arrival in Caesarea with Agrippa II
keyEvents.description: Berenice came with her brother King Agrippa II to Caesarea to greet the new governor Festus.

keyEvents.title: Hearing Paul's Defense Speech
keyEvents.description: Berenice was present in the courtroom with Agrippa II and Festus when Paul presented his defense and testified about his conversion and ministry.

keyEvents.title: Witness to Paul's Testimony
keyEvents.description: She heard Paul tell about his meeting with the risen Christ and his call to preach to the Gentiles.

keyEvents.title: Conversation about Paul's innocence
keyEvents.description: After Paul's defense speech, Berenike withdrew together with Agrippa and Festus, and they agreed that Paul had done nothing deserving death or imprisonment.
